findings.namedBuyers: Carys J. Craig: York/Osgoode Professor, ATRIP Executive Committee member and local hosting lead identified by IP Osgoode’s congress handover announcement; strongest evidenced local routing contact for accommodation and ancillary-event questions. Public faculty email: ccraig@osgoode.yorku.ca. Estelle Derclaye: ATRIP President, identified in the 2027 host-site welcome letter; senior association-side relationship and decision-routing contact. ATRIP publishes admin@atrip.org for submission assistance; this is an administrative routing channel, not Derclaye’s personal email or a verified housing desk. Neither person is verified as a hotel-contract signatory or procurement manager.
findings.futureEdition: Officially confirmed, strictly in-person 45th Annual Congress, 27–30 June 2027, hosted by Osgoode Hall Law School, York University, Toronto. These are activity dates, not article dates, and fall within the requested horizon. The submission-form heading incorrectly says 2026; the official York host page, ATRIP announcement and 2027 call-for-papers PDF consistently say 2027 and take precedence. No officially announced 2028 host, dates or venue was located.
findings.hotelProductFit: Inference using the supplied hotel specifications: Radisson Blu Toronto Downtown could accommodate a subset of delegates/speakers, executives or a small side meeting, not be assumed to house the entire congress. Its 157 rooms and approximately 240-theatre/224-banquet largest-room capacity do not support a promise to host the whole event: the historical 2026 congress had around 250 participants, while 2027 scale is unknown. A selective block within the hotel’s supplied approximately 15–109 peak-room target is a prospecting parameter, not published event demand. Downtown Dundas activity provides a plausible city-hotel connection, but Keele-campus sessions weaken the Harbourfront location advantage and require transport planning. Resort positioning is not relevant to the announced university/city format. Full congress meeting space is already announced elsewhere. Catering/reception feasibility must be checked internally; restaurant/lounge operation and catering capability are not established here.
findings.venueCommitments: The edition-specific York site names TWO venues: Osgoode Professional Development, 26th Floor, 1 Dundas Street West, Toronto; and Osgoode Hall Law School of York University, 4700 Keele Street, Toronto, Ontario, Canada. Both are within Toronto proper. The Dundas venue is downtown; the Keele-campus venue is outside the hotel’s Harbourfront/downtown/MTCC/Exhibition Place core territory. Neither is a hotel, MTCC or Exhibition Place. Venue publication establishes the announced host venues, not proof of a signed contract. Day-by-day allocation is not published in the material reviewed.
findings.historicalRotation: Verified sequence: 41st Congress, University of Tokyo, Tokyo, 9–12 July 2023; 42nd, Luiss University, Rome, 30 June–3 July 2024; 43rd, University of Copenhagen, Copenhagen, 22–25 June 2025; 44th, University of São Paulo, São Paulo, 28 June–1 July 2026; 45th announced for Toronto, 27–30 June 2027. ATRIP explicitly states that congresses are hosted each year in a different country. Annual recurrence and international rotation are verified; a return to Toronto is not.
findings.accommodationSourcing: Unknown for 2027. No edition-specific housing bureau, host hotel, recommended-hotel list, negotiated block, booking link, hotel RFP or lodging commitment was found in the official York/ATRIP congress materials reviewed. Consequently there are no verified 2027 hotel names to report. York states “Registration Opening Soon”; ATRIP states “Online registration for the Congress is expected to be available by early 2027.” These quotes concern registration, not proof that hotel sourcing is open. No published 2027 attendance, peak rooms or room-night figure was found. The 2026 archive reports “more than 170 speakers and around 250 participants”; this is historical scale only, not a 2027 forecast or room count.
findings.organizationStructure: ATRIP is an international academic association/society for intellectual-property teaching and research, governed through its president and executive committee. ATRIP is the event association; Osgoode Hall Law School, York University is the local academic host, with Osgoode Professional Development and the Keele-campus law school as announced venues. No appointed PCO, DMC, housing agency or commercial hotel buyer was identified in the reviewed edition-specific material. Do not conflate the association, host, venues and contracting buyer.
findings.competitiveLimitations: Announced academic venues constrain capture of core meeting-space business. No incumbent hotel, exclusivity clause, contracted room allocation, sellout or unmet overflow demand is evidenced. Absence of published hotel information must not be interpreted as uncommitted inventory. Inference: hotels closer to the eventual session venue could have a location advantage, particularly for Keele-campus days; no specific competitor commitment is asserted.
findings.recommendedSalesAction: Approach Carys Craig through her public York faculty email and request introduction to the person handling 2027 accommodation and social-event logistics. Ask whether any hotel blocks, university residences or housing agent are already appointed; request every hotel name, booking terms, expected attendance, room pickup/peak requirement, venue-by-day schedule, transfer expectations and any unplaced dinner/reception needs. Offer a limited delegate/speaker block only if need and procurement access are confirmed; propose a small side event only after hotel catering/restaurant capability is verified internally. Use ATRIP admin to route an association-side enquiry to President Estelle Derclaye if needed. Recheck the official congress site when registration is expected to open in early 2027; do not wait to introduce the hotel. Keep qualification conditional; final qualification remains with ORS.
findings.currentEditionAccessibility: 2027 is a confirmed upcoming Toronto edition, but commercial accessibility is unconfirmed. Registration is announced for early 2027; no published hotel tender or lodging procurement route was located. The defensible route now is an exploratory enquiry to the local host, not a claim of open sourcing, secured overflow or available catering business.
findings.futureCompetitiveCapturePotential: International annual rotation is explicitly established, but no 2028 edition announcement or repeat Toronto cycle was located. Inference: develop the local Osgoode relationship for possible Toronto academic groups and consider a 2027 lodging proposal only if the host confirms a need. Do not project annual Toronto room demand or label 2028 as a confirmed competitive-capture opportunity.
